kjv: the caul that is above the liver
note: yoteret is the appendage (caudate lobe) of the liver, not the caul (omentum).
ishsheh was traditionally linked to esh "fire"; many now connect it with a word for gift/food (Ugaritic itt), since it is used even of offerings not burned.

mine: the fat tail... the right thigh
note: alyah is the fat tail of the sheep; shoq is the leg/thigh, not the shoulder (also 29:27).
minchah here is the flour-and-oil offering of 29:40; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, but modern readers take it as animal flesh.
zar here means anyone not of the priestly family (a layperson), not a foreigner as "stranger" suggests.
